clue.text: Like inflamed viewer's false statement about reptile

definitions.meaning: first meaning: describing a red, irritated eye, the viewer being the eye
second meaning, read as two words with the apostrophe-s: reptiles are cold-blooded, so saying a reptile's blood is warm would be untrue

explanation.surface: Someone with a sore eye tells a fib about a snake or lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of viewer's does double duty: split the answer as BLOOD'S HOT, a claim that is false of a cold-blooded reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshot describes eyes reddened by swollen blood vessels, and an eye is the organ a viewer sees with.

clue.text: Girl brought up overlooking area in Dutch city

parts.note: brought up, as a child is raised
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A girl raised in the Netherlands looks out over a district of her home town.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a definition at each end: Breda is a girl's name, common in Ireland, and a city in the Netherlands. 'Overlooking' places the first piece above the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Breda is both a city in North Brabant in the southern Netherlands and an Irish female first name.

clue.text: Work with a business community — there's a lack of transparency

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
taken as written
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Doing deals with financiers, one complains, means nothing is open and above board.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the square mile of London where banks and finance houses are based.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is the quality of being opaque, not letting light through, so it is the absence of transparency.

clue.text: Flower is squashed in time

indicators.note: something squashed is crushed out of its shape, so these letters lose their order
in tells us the jumbled pair of letters sits inside the word for a period

parts.note: a day is a unit of time
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A bloom gets crushed just at the moment it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: The daisy is a common flower with white petals around a yellow centre.

clue.text: Rodent seen in Nottingham's terrible

indicators.note: seen in says the answer can be spotted inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the city's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A rat-like creature has been spotted in an awful part of Nottingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small burrowing rodent often kept as a pet.

clue.text: Somehow isn't leader, last in marches to depart?

definitions.text: Somehow isn't leader, last in marches to depart?

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be put together in any order
to depart means to leave, so the named letter goes out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: 'last in' keeps only the last letter of 'marches'

parts.note: the final letter of marches

explanation.surface: A marcher at the back of the parade is anything but the one in front.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S from the fodder and rearrange the rest. The whole clue is also the definition: someone who is not the leader, last in the marching line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender is the one who comes last in a line or race, the very opposite of a leader.

clue.text: A medical practitioner returning with additional notes

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the words are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a doc is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor comes back carrying more paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like a doctor's written notes, but here they are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is a closing passage added to the end of a piece of music, extra notes after the main structure.

clue.text: Nautical item is on top of vessel, not bottom

indicators.note: not bottom asks for the lowest letter of this down entry's piece to be left off

parts.note: caps means sits on top of, as a lid does
a tank is a container for liquid

explanation.surface: A ship's fitting sits on top of a boat, not at its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which suits the nautical surface, but it is a container for liquids.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship's deck used for winding in cables and anchor ropes.

clue.text: Is girl taken in by naughty lad getting the boot?

indicators.note: taken in by means received inside, so the first pieces go within the other letters
naughty means misbehaving, so these letters will not stay in their proper places

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged around the rest
taken as written
Miss is the title of an unmarried girl

explanation.surface: A girl is taken in by a bad boy, and asks whether she is being given the boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the boot is an idiom for being sacked, and dismissal is the act of being sent away from a job.

clue.text: Plant providing semiconducting material — mass turned out

indicators.note: turned out means expelled, so the named letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a metalloid element used in transistors
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A plant yields a chemical used in electronics, once its bulk has been cleared away.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the third letter of the element to leave the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The geranium is a common flowering garden and pot plant, also called cranesbill.

clue.text: This writer's nonsense is naughty

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: I am, shortened
pish is an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish

explanation.surface: A writer confesses that his own rubbish is rather wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, so 'This writer's' is I'M, 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish means mischievous like an imp, which is playfully naughty.

clue.text: Elusive cat mum lost in pit

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so the named piece disappears from the name

parts.note: Macavity the Mystery Cat, who is never there, in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A cat that never shows itself, and its mother, go missing down a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: Macavity is the cat in Eliot's poems (and the musical Cats) famous for never being at the scene of a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is a hollow space, just as a pit is a hole in the ground or a hollow in a surface.

clue.text: Tennis — it is played in Chinese city

indicators.note: is played suggests the letters are moved about freely like pieces in a game

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tennis: it is a sport people take up in a city in China.
explanation.walkthrough: Tientsin is the older Western spelling of Tianjin, the port city near Beijing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tientsin is the old romanised name of Tianjin, a major city in northern China.

clue.text: Appealed audibly to the Lord, as profited from in an exploitative manner

definitions.text: profited from in an exploitative manner

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so it is the sound of the phrase that counts, not its spelling

parts.note: appealing to God is praying, the sense the next words complete
completes the phrase: one who appealed to the Lord prayed

explanation.surface: A pious hypocrite prays to God while taking advantage of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' sits inside the phrase it acts on. To prey on people is to exploit them.
explanation.definitionFit: Preyed on means exploited or took advantage of someone vulnerable, as a predator hunts its victims.

clue.text: England batter sure to be restricted and unable to blossom?

parts.note: Joe Root, England's leading Test run-scorer
as in bound to happen, certain

explanation.surface: An England cricketer, sure to be hemmed in, cannot make his runs flow.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root is a celebrated English Test cricket batsman. The question mark flags that the definition describes a pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootbound plant has filled its pot with roots, so it is cramped and cannot flourish or flower.

clue.text: Bit of a letter, final bit in rambling screed

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: the end is the final bit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small part of a letter is the last bit of a long-winded rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence, which suits screed, but here it is a printed character.
explanation.definitionFit: A descender is the part of a lowercase letter such as g or p that drops below the line.

clue.text: Endures horrible son showing incivility

indicators.note: horrible things are a mess, so the letters come out disordered

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent puts up with a dreadful boy who is always impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is lack of politeness, which is what incivility means.

clue.text: Trick female employed, making one puzzled

parts.note: a con is a swindle
F is the abbreviation for female
used means put to work

explanation.surface: A woman hired to carry out a scam leaves someone baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Confused and puzzled both describe someone who cannot make sense of something.

clue.text: Vagrant having minimum of food subsequently eating egg

indicators.note: the minimum of something is its least part, so only one letter is kept, the opening one

parts.note: the opening letter of food

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the following item goes within the word before it

parts.note: later means afterwards
O is shaped like an egg

explanation.surface: A tramp with barely any food later tucks into an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: O stands for egg because of its shape, as in a duck's egg for nought in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A floater is someone who drifts from place to place without settling, like a vagrant.

clue.text: Falsely accused prisoner — uncontrollable fury dies when one is released

indicators.note: uncontrollable means wild and unruly, so these letters scatter out of order
is released means set free, so the named letter leaves the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wrongly jailed man's anger subsides when he is set free.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from the eight letters and rearrange the remaining seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Dreyfus was the French army officer wrongly convicted of treason in 1894 and imprisoned on Devil's Island.

clue.text: Flyers did what they do, endless game of chance

indicators.note: endless means without a finish, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, Britain's military airmen
what flyers do is fly, and in the past tense they flew

explanation.surface: Pilots carried out their usual job, an unending gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force. 'They' points back to the flyers.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle is a lottery in which numbered tickets are drawn at random for prizes, a game of chance.

clue.text: Top viral infection expert achieving through chance

parts.note: influenza is caused by a virus
a king is the top figure in a field
rounds out the phrase: a top expert on a subject is its king

explanation.surface: A leading virologist gets results by sheer luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Top viral infection expert' as a flu king, a leading authority on flu. The expert surface tempts solvers towards names such as Fleming or Fauci.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluke something is to succeed by luck rather than skill, so fluking is achieving by chance.

clue.text: Let oboes play like serpents?

indicators.note: play suggests free movement, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to have woodwind players perform as if they were snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: A serpent is an old snake-shaped bass wind instrument, now little played, not a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: The serpent has been replaced by the tuba and other brass, so it is an outdated, disused instrument.

clue.text: Fruit reported — heavy hanging masses

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the word is used

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit, and here in the plural

explanation.surface: Heavy fruit droops on the branches, they say.
explanation.walkthrough: A plumb is a lead weight hung on a line to find a true vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbs are the lead weights on plumb lines, weighty bobs that hang straight down.

clue.text: Lever journalist into China?

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the first piece is set within the other

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Does a reporter want to move to the Far East?
explanation.walkthrough: China is not the country but Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal is a foot-operated lever, as on a bicycle or piano.

clue.text: Surrounded foe finally in defeat

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the following word

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of foe

explanation.surface: An enemy, ringed by troops, at last goes down to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Beset means attacked or hemmed in on all sides, which is what surrounded describes.

clue.text: Travelled over water, getting kicked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: went in a flat boat pushed with a pole
second meaning: struck with the foot, as a ball dropped from the hands

explanation.surface: Someone crossing a river ends up being given a kicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting kicked' must be read as an adjective-like past participle: kicked, as a ball is punted downfield.
explanation.definitionFit: To punt is both to propel a flat-bottomed boat with a pole and to kick a dropped ball before it lands.

clue.text: Most fastidious theologian that is participating in Lent?

indicators.note: participating in means taking part within, so the earlier pieces go inside

parts.note: Lent is a season of fasting
DD is Doctor of Divinity
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A fussy cleric takes his part in the Lenten observance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' here is not the past of lend but the Christian period of fasting before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Faddiest means having the most fads or whims, so most fussy or fastidious about things.

clue.text: Group of actors back for a month

indicators.note: back signals reading in the opposite direction from usual

parts.note: the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school

explanation.surface: A theatre company returns home for a month-long run.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's leading drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is the sixth month of the Jewish civil year, falling in February and March.

clue.text: Hasten to land, with a little help in the dark

definitions.text: a little help in the dark

parts.note: to rush is to hurry
to light on or alight is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: Hurrying to come ashore, someone is grateful for some guidance at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Light as a verb, like alight, means to come down and settle, as a bird does.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushlight is a candle made of rush pith dipped in fat, giving only a feeble light.
